claims.text: Mechanical-property differences among the single-phase FCC alloys arise from composition-dependent local lattice distortions and chemical short-range order.
Local lattice distortions and chemical short-range order modulate dislocation mobility during deformation.
The baseline and selected quaternary and ternary alloys will be prepared as single-phase FCC materials using consistent thermomechanical processing.
Removing or substituting elements in equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni changes local lattice distortion and chemical short-range order while the FCC phase is retained.
The alloys will be tensile-tested at room temperature at an approximately fixed strain rate of 10^-3 s^-1 under otherwise identical processing and testing conditions.
TEM, high-resolution STEM, diffraction, and atom-probe tomography can characterize the proposed local lattice distortion and chemical-ordering mediators.
Local lattice distortions are established by atomic-size mismatch.
Chemical short-range order is established by solute-solute interactions.
Changes in elemental composition produce different atomic-size mismatches and bonding environments.
Different atomic-size mismatches and bonding environments generate distinct degrees of local lattice distortion and chemical short-range order.
Local lattice distortion and chemical short-range order affect dislocation nucleation and glide by impeding or facilitating dislocation motion.
Changes in dislocation nucleation and glide alter yield strength and work-hardening behavior.
Relative to equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni, alloys with greater local lattice distortion are predicted to have higher yield strength.
Relative to the baseline, alloys with greater local lattice distortion are predicted to exhibit altered work-hardening rates.
Alloys with lower local lattice distortion are predicted to have lower strength than the equiatomic quinary baseline.
The proposed relationship is restricted to single-phase FCC alloys with controlled grain size and no secondary phases or dominant transformation effects.
Traditional solid-solution strengthening and other mechanisms may complicate attribution of strength solely to local distortion and short-range order.
